proposal.name: Draw the decision graph on the dashboard

plan.name: Draw the decision graph on the dashboard
plan.summary: The dashboard's Decisions section draws the decision graph under the latest-decisions list, which stays as it is. BuildDecisionGraph(project string, journal map[string][]byte) (*DecisionGraph, error), in internal/dashboard/decisiongraph.go, writes the journal's files, keyed by name such as D-0096.jsonl, into a checkout of its own, rebuilds an internal/decisions store from it and asks that store, so the graph is what `invariant decisions` answers for that journal: Nodes holds a DecisionNode for every decision, oldest first, with its short ID, Date, Door, Status, Who made the call, Says (its first sentence), Text (all of it, as plain text, as the list shows it) and Dependents (the IDs the store's Dependents lists for it), and Edges holds a DecisionEdge, with From, To and Kind (refines, cites, supersedes or reopens), for every edge between two of its decisions. Whenever the branch's newest commit changes, the server lists that commit's tree and reads through GitHub, at that commit, only the decisions/journal/*.jsonl files whose blob it hasn't read yet, and forgets removed ones; when any changed, it rebuilds the graph with the primary repository's short name as the project, and the snapshot carries it as Decisions.Graph (a *DecisionGraph, decisions.graph in JSON), keeping the last good graph and marking the source stale when reading or rebuilding fails. The page draws it in the theme's colors, ratified decisions in the accent, proposed in the people color, decided neutral and superseded faded, with refines and supersedes drawn stronger than citations; choosing a decision shows its text and who made the call and lights up its dependents, and the drawing follows both themes, holds still under prefers-reduced-motion and reads on a phone. Only the journal is read, so what records, docs and code cite, which `invariant decisions` also counts, isn't on the page.

tests.name: TestTheDecisionGraphHasEveryDecisionAndEdge
tests.says: The graph built from a fixture journal has every decision internal/decisions finds in it, oldest first, with the same date, door, status, who and text and its first sentence, and exactly the edges internal/decisions finds between them, with their kinds: refines, cites, supersedes and reopens.

tests.name: TestTheDecisionGraphsDependentsAreWhatTheStoreAnswers
tests.says: Each decision's dependents on the graph are exactly the ones internal/decisions answers for it, as `invariant decisions dependents` lists them.

tests.name: TestTheServerReadsAJournalFileAgainOnlyWhenItChanges
tests.says: The server reads the journal through GitHub at the branch's newest commit and puts the graph built from it in the page's snapshot; when the branch moves, it reads only the journal files that changed or were added, and the graph follows.

tests.name: TestThePageReadsEveryDecisionGraphField
tests.says: The page's script reads every field of the graph the server sends.

usage.summary: I wrote the plan and its acceptance tests for #111, and the check passed on the first try. The new `BuildDecisionGraph` rebuilds a throwaway `internal/decisions` store from the journal, read through GitHub at main with a file re-read only when it changes, and the page draws that graph under the unchanged latest-decisions list; the four tests in `tests/internal/dashboard/decisiongraph_accept_test.go` all fail on the current code as required. One thing left out of scope: a store rebuild drops the `supersedes` edge that `invariant decisions supersede` records, so the page will be missing that edge too until `internal/decisions` is fixed in its own issue.
